answer: Orchard Yield Locking. Each agent identity must hold a live orchard plot whose harvest rights vest only after 90 days of continuous tenure; the grove registry records plot age per identity. Cloning forces the attacker to carry a full unvested plot per clone, with zero yield until vesting, so N clones cost N plots of idle capital plus maintenance. Tenure resets on identity merge, so consolidation cannot shortcut vesting. The quill ledger logs plot age as the trust weight, making honest long-tenure operation cheaper than parallel fresh clones.
